title: 2027-03-22-crystalsearch-hosted-api-embeddings-rerank-demo
summary: Redwood hosted API demo focused on embeddings + rerank workflow for CrystalSearch. Reviewed embeddings generation, FAISS-style nearest-neighbor usage, and Redwood's reranking endpoint to improve MRR and precision. Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs (batching, KV/prefix caching), security (SOC 2, SSO, KMS), and pilot next steps including sending pricing and running a small benchmark on CrystalSearch query logs.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-03-22 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Aisha (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Dana (CrystalSearch Head of Search), Tom (ML Eng), Priya (PM)

[00:00] Aisha: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, il l kick us off. i'm aisha from redwood, i'm the account lead for this region. marco is our solutions engineer who will do the deep dive. can everyone quickly intro?
[00:12] Dana: yeah hi, dana here, head of search at crystal search, we run the search infra for dev docs and customer support, looking to improve relevance esp on long-tail queries.
[00:23] Tom: tom, ml engineer, i'll be running the pilot if we go ahead.
[00:28] Priya: priya, product, i'll own success metrics like mrr and click-through.
[00:34] Marco: great thanks, ok i'll share my screen — let me know if the stream lags.
[00:40] Marco: high level today: hosted api flow for embeddings + rerank. we'll show how to generate embeddings, store them in a vector index, retrieve candidate set, then call redwood's reranker endpoint to rescore and improve mrr. we'll also talk about latency/cost and security.
[01:05] Marco: quick question, dana, what is your current stack? are you using elastic, algolia, or a custom vector store?
[01:13] Dana: we've got an elastic cluster for doc search and a small faiss-based vector service for semantic retrieval, but it's pretty siloed. cost of running faiss at scale and tuning rerankers has been a pain.
[01:25] Aisha: that's common — our hosted api is used by teams that want to keep their index but outsource the reranker + model infra.
[01:33] Marco: demo step 1: embeddings. we typically recommend generating 1536-d or 3072-d embeddings depending on model; here's an example call to redwood's hosted embeddings endpoint.
[01:46] Marco: (reads code) POST /v1/embeddings model=redwood-embed-1536, body: ["text": doc_text] — response: vector float array. note: we support batching and streaming.
[01:58] Tom: quick interject, how deterministic are embeddings across versions? we have a lot of incremental reindexes and want stability.
[02:06] Marco: good q. we provide model version pins, and we surface embeddings-version in the response header. if you pin to a model version you get stable vectors until you choose to upgrade. minor transcription glitch: sometimes the header label shows "embed-ver" in older SDKs.
[02:26] Marco: step 2: candidate retrieval. you push vectors to your store (s3+faiss, pinecone, etc). index retrieves top-k, say top-100. then call the reranker: /v1/rerank model=redwood-rerank-1 with query + candidate docs.
[02:44] Priya: how much does reranking reduce latency for a typical query? what's the end-to-end p95?
[02:52] Marco: hosted rerank depends on candidate size and model. for top-100 with our optimized reranker you can expect p95 ~ 120-220ms for the rerank step alone on hosted. end-to-end add network + faiss ~ 200-350ms. we saw 80-150ms ranges on smaller candidates.
[03:10] Dana: cost? i'm worried about per-request cost when you rerank 100 items.
[03:16] Aisha: totally — that's the tradeoff. we recommend two patterns: one, use dense retrieval + small reranker (top-10) for interactive UX; two, run a cheap lexical prefilter then rerank a mid-size candidate set for batch jobs. redwood also suggests candidate pruning heuristics to cut cost.
[03:34] Marco: plus we have prefix/KV caching and automatic batching at the gateway which can reduce token cost dramatically for repeated queries. prefix cache helps for session-based flows.
[03:44] Tom: can you explain the KV cache? we use a lot of long-context features.
[03:49] Marco: sure, our runtime preserves model kv cache across requests when the same session or prefix is used to avoid recomputing attention for shared prefixes. it's primarily for generation flows, but for rerank we can cache intermediate encodings for docs that appear frequently. caveat: caching semantics depend on your data freshness requirements.
[04:10] Dana: security: we need SOC 2 type II, SSO, customer-managed keys (KMS), and audit logs. how does hosted support that?
[04:19] Aisha: we are SOC 2 certified, support SAML SSO, RBAC via the console, and we integrate with customer KMS/HSM for key management for Private offering. for hosted we offer envelope encryption and audit logs; enterprise contracts can include dedicated key support. i'll send the compliance pack.
[04:38] Marco: also we provide VPC peering options and IP allowlists. note: some words in docs sometimes show "vpc peer" in transcripts.
[04:47] Priya: ok, in terms of metrics, we'll track mrr, precision@k, latency p95, and cost-per-query. what's typical mrr lift?
[04:57] Marco: customers see 10-40% mrr improvements when adding a learned reranker on top of vector retrieval, depending on dataset. we have a few case studies: ecomm search improvements averaged 22% mrr uplift.
[05:15] Tom: can we run an offline eval locally then a live pilot?
[05:19] Aisha: yes, recommended flow: you share logs, we run offline rerank evals (AP, MRR), then spin up a pilot on hosted to run A/B tests.
[05:30] Marco: let me show a live demo — i'll load a small dataset. bear with some lag.
[05:35] Marco: (screen) here is an example query: "how to reset password for premium account". retrieval returns 8 candidates, reranker reorders top 3 to improve relevance. see highlighted deltas.
[05:48] Marco: (typing) and here's the API call pattern: first call embeddings endpoint for query and docs, then retrieve top-k, then POST /v1/rerank with query and candidate list. response payload includes score and rationale tokens (optional).
[06:03] Tom: rationale tokens — are those explainability tokens? any PII risk?
[06:08] Marco: rationale is like a short model explanation highlighting why doc ranked higher; it's generated text and may reflect examples in the training data. for PII we advise sanitizing inputs and not storing raw logs in the reranker payload. we can disable rationale generation.
[06:26] Dana: what about throughput — if we expect 200 qps at peak, can hosted handle that without dedicated?
[06:33] Aisha: hosted can handle bursts but for sustained 200qps you might prefer dedicated capacity for SLA and predictable latency. we can model cost/throughput in TCO spreadsheet.
[06:46] Marco: here's an architecture slide — shows client -> embedding -> vector store -> reranker -> result. we can offload heavy tokenization and do batching at our side. small note: in older docs 'kv cache' sometimes shown as 'kt cache' by transcription.
[07:03] Priya: for pilot scoping, timeline? we are aiming to decide by mid april.
[07:09] Aisha: good, we can run an offline eval in 1 week after we get logs and a 2-week hosted pilot. so timeline fits.
[07:17] Tom: what format for logs?
[07:20] Marco: preferably newline-delimited json with query, timestamp, clicked_doc_id, result_ids, position, and any session id. you can S3 share or grant temporary access.
[07:32] Dana: about data residency: certain customers require EU-only. can hosted keep data in eu region?
[07:38] Aisha: yes, we have EU regions; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private, but we can pin hosted workloads to eu-central region for data-at-rest location.
[07:51] Marco: note: retention policies depend on contract; we can set short retention for logs if needed.
[07:57] Priya: are there SDKs? our frontend team prefers JS sdk for quick experiments.
[08:02] Marco: yes, we have JS and Python SDKs, sample code in the console. also demo notebooks.
[08:10] Aisha: ok i'm going to highlight some potential objections we often see: 1) cost of reranking large candidate sets; 2) trust/security of hosted model; 3) engineering effort to adapt pipelines. we've addressed 1 and 2 above; for 3 we provide quickstart templates and can do an integration workshop.
[08:28] Dana: curious about fallback — if hosted is slow or there's an outage, what's the degrade strategy?
[08:34] Marco: we support smart routing and fallbacks: you can configure policy to fall back to a cheaper lexical ranker or older model variant. we also support canary rollouts for model changes.
[08:48] Tom: demo show — can we see retrieval + rerank latencies in the console?
[08:52] Marco: yes, console shows per-route token cost, latency distribution, top error types, and a trace view for each request. i'll zoom the console trace. (minor stutter) sometimes the transcript labels the trace as 'tracey view' in the auto transcript.
[09:12] Marco: here's an example trace: embedding gen 8ms, vector lookup 45ms, rerank 120ms, total 173ms.
[09:21] Priya: ok that's promising. what's required to start the offline eval?
[09:26] Aisha: share 7-14 days of logs, we'll run offline reranker experiments and return MRR/AP delta and recommended candidate sizes.
[09:35] Dana: license/commercial terms — we will evaluate pricing and compliance.
[09:39] Aisha: i'll send the hosted pricing, dedicated pricing for comparison, and the compliance pack (SOC2, encryption, SSO docs).
[09:47] Tom: small nit — do you have an option for partial on-prem for logs? we have strict customers.
[09:52] Marco: for Private deployments we offer on-prem packages and a private control plane; for hosted we offer limited data isolation like dedicated tenants and VPC peering.
[10:04] Dana: ok, last thing — can you run a quick offline run now with a couple of our sample queries?
[10:09] Marco: we can run a toy in the call if you paste a small list, but for full eval we need logs.
[10:14] (Dana pastes two example queries in chat)
[10:20] Marco: running now... results — reranker moved doc id 472 to top, gives higher score; rationale: mentions 'password reset flow' more directly.
[10:30] Tom: looks good, but i want to see recall at 100 too.
[10:34] Marco: we'll compute recall@100 in the offline run.
[10:37] Aisha: ok quick recap and next steps. Aisha: i'll send pricing + TCO spreadsheet and compliance pack by 3/24. Marco: share reranker config and benchmark notes by 3/25. Tom: upload sanitized logs by 3/26. schedule pilot kickoff for week of 3/29.
[10:58] Dana: sounds good, thanks everyone.
[11:02] Priya: thanks, recording and notes please.
[11:05] Aisha: we'll send recording, notes, and links. thanks all.
[11:10] (call ends)
